_about: E11 full-episode-only fragment (the full_only.json equivalent for E11, named mistake.json per the brief section 15). Consequence-flip episode (ENG-04): in place of an attack half, the learner makes four everyday choices in a safe sandbox (the `mistake` stage), then a montage flip shows where each led. These keys are pasted into scenarios/awareness_e11_misdirected_data/scenario.json.erb (the FULL shell) ONLY; the generated defend-only shell never carries them. None is in the fragment-erb parity comparison (the mistake and flip blocks are episode-level; strings.flipMontageByChoice is erb-only, added to STRINGS_ERB_ONLY_OK by ENG-04). Shapes follow test/js/fixtures/social_awareness/clean_mistake.json, scripts/validate_social/awareness.rb mistake_checks/montage_line_checks, and public/break_escape/js/minigames/episode-runner/consequence-sandbox.js. All people fictional; see defend.json and BRAND_ADDITIONS.md.

_notes.mistake: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.mistake (ENG-04). The sandbox of four everyday choices, unscored. Exactly one safe:true option per beat (the approved route); the safe option is NOT first every time (consequence-sandbox radios are shown in authored order, so the position is varied: safe first in caller_bernadette and marketing_export, safe second in overtime_sheet and redaction_send). flipBeat is overtime_sheet, the episode's title case (the misdirected email with the health notes), quoted back as the montage headline.
_notes.flip: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.flip (ENG-04). mode 'montage' makes the flip replay the sandbox choices instead of looking for a sent message; required when stages lists 'mistake' (awareness.rb). flipHeading ('Six months later') lives in defend.json strings, shared by both variants.
_notes.flipMontageByChoice: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.strings.flipMontageByChoice (ENG-04), FULL shell only. Keyed beatId then optionId; a line is authored for BOTH options of every beat (brief section 10a), so ENG-04's unsafe-option fallback never fires for E11. The 'Your choice' / 'the version where it was taken instead' framing is in the text, not applied by the engine. Erb-only: it must NOT appear in the defend-only shell (parity test); add flipMontageByChoice to STRINGS_ERB_ONLY_OK in test/js/social-awareness-fragment-erb-parity.test.mjs (ENG-04 owns this).

beats.situation: Carol rings the desk: "I'm Bernadette's sister, it's her fiftieth and I'm planning a surprise. Which school is she cleaning at today, and what time does she finish?" Bernadette Lyons is one of Carrholme's cleaners.

options.label: Offer to pass a message to Bernadette
Tell her it is Ashgrove Primary and she finishes at three, as it is a surprise

beats.situation: Shauna asks you to send this month's overtime sheet to Sam in Payroll. The sheet lists nine staff, their hours, and a notes column ("hospital appointment", "back injury", "union meeting"). Typing "Sam" offers Sam Whitlow (Hollinsbrook House) first, with an 'External recipient' chip, and Sam Whitaker (Payroll) second.

options.label: Send it to the first Sam the address box offers, to save time
Check the address, then send it to Sam Whitaker

beats.situation: Martin, the Sales Director, messages you: "We're launching a cleaning service for families. Export the family contacts from the claims system and I'll send them a discount."

options.label: Ask the data protection lead before exporting anything
Export the family contacts for Martin, since he is the Sales Director

beats.situation: Shauna: "Send Mr Hale a copy of the incident report for his complaint." The one-page report names Edna Hale's missing cardigan and the date (fine to send), and also Albert Finch (Room 14, with a continence-care note), Pauline Grant (Room 9), and a driver's personal mobile.

options.label: Send the report as it is, since Shauna asked for a copy to go to Mr Hale
Take out the other residents, the care note and the mobile, then send

flipMontageByChoice._use: The full text of the montage lines. Lives at social.awarenessEpisode.strings.flipMontageByChoice in the full erb.

overtime_sheet.send_wrong_sam: The overtime sheet, with the back-injury and union-meeting notes, sat in a care home manager's inbox for three days before anyone noticed. Three days the data protection lead never had, to warn the staff and limit the harm.
overtime_sheet.check_then_send: The version where it went to the first Sam instead: staff health notes reached someone outside Carrholme, unnoticed for three days. A glance at the address stopped it here.

caller_bernadette.give_details: Two weeks on, a stranger was waiting for Bernadette outside her school. The birthday-surprise call was how he learned where a lone worker would be, and when.
caller_bernadette.take_message: The version where the school and the time were given out: a stranger learned where a lone worker would be. Offering to pass a message gave the caller nothing.

marketing_export.export_list: A month on, three families complained and one wrote to the regulator. The contacts had been given to sort out a lost cardigan, not to hear about offers.
marketing_export.ask_dpo: The version where the list was exported: families who had given their details to sort a claim got a marketing email, and complained. Asking first turned it into a proper sign-up box.

redaction_send.send_as_is: Mr Hale opened the report and read another resident's continence-care note and a driver's mobile number. One mistake, two more people's data exposed.
redaction_send.redact_first: The version where the report went as it was: another resident's care note and a driver's mobile reached a stranger. Taking the extra details out first left only what Mr Hale was owed.
